Primitive Random Bits

Source: R/primitives.R
prim_sample_bits.Rd

Draws random bits from the active random state (see nv_set_seed()) with the ThreeFry-2x32 counter-based generator of Salmon et al. (2011), and advances that random state by one step.

See the Random Number Generation article for more details.

Usage

prim_sample_bits(shape, dtype)

Arguments

shape

(integer())
Shape of the result.

dtype

(character(1) | DataType)
An unsigned integer data type: "ui8", "ui16", "ui32" or "ui64".

Value

(arrayish)
The random bits, of data type dtype and shape shape. Every value is made from an encrypted 64-bit block of its own: a "ui64" value is the block, and a narrower value the xor of the block's two 32-bit words, truncated to its low bits, as JAX's jax.random.bits() does by default. The value at a position thus does not depend on the number of values drawn, so a draw of 3 is the start of a draw of 6. The draws fill shape in row-major order, as JAX's do, so a draw of c(2, 3) is not a draw of 6 filled into c(2, 3) in R's column-major order.

Random State

The draws come from the active random state: the global random state (see nv_set_seed()), or the random state that with_nv_rng_state() or local_nv_rng_state() make the default for a scope. They advance it in place.

Implemented Rules

  • stablehlo

References

Salmon J, Moraes M, Dror R, Shaw D (2011). “Parallel Random Numbers: As Easy as 1, 2, 3.” In Proceedings of the 2011 International Conference for High Performance Computing, Networking, Storage and Analysis. doi:10.1145/2063384.2063405 .

Claessen K, Pałka M (2013). “Splittable Pseudorandom Number Generators using Cryptographic Hashing.” In Proceedings of the 2013 ACM SIGPLAN Symposium on Haskell, 47–58. doi:10.1145/2503778.2503784 .

Bradbury J, Frostig R, Hawkins P, Johnson M, Katariya Y, Leary C, Maclaurin D, Necula G, Paszke A, VanderPlas J, Wanderman-Milne S, Zhang Q (2018). JAX: composable transformations of Python+NumPy programs. Version 0.11.2, http://github.com/jax-ml/jax.

See also

nv_runif(), nv_rnorm()

Examples

nv_get_rng_state()
#> <AnvlRngState> key 0x000000000000002a, counter 0x0000000000000003
prim_sample_bits(2L, "ui32")
#> AnvlArray
#>  1.6708e+09
#>  3.6823e+08
#> [ CPUui32{2} ] 
# The counter is incremented by 1
nv_get_rng_state()
#> <AnvlRngState> key 0x000000000000002a, counter 0x0000000000000004
# A random state of its own is drawn from within with_nv_rng_state():
custom_rng <- nv_rng_state(1L)
custom_rng
#> <AnvlRngState> key 0x0000000000000001, counter 0x0000000000000000
with_nv_rng_state(custom_rng, prim_sample_bits(2L, "ui32"))
#> AnvlArray
#>  3.0177e+09
#>  1.0086e+09
#> [ CPUui32{2} ] 
# And it is still updated
custom_rng
#> <AnvlRngState> key 0x0000000000000001, counter 0x0000000000000001
# And does not affect the global RNG
nv_get_rng_state()
#> <AnvlRngState> key 0x000000000000002a, counter 0x0000000000000004
